source.title: More Than Seeing: Vision as Scalable Anchors in Native Multimodal Pre-Training
source.authors: Haoyuan Wu; Ao-Qi Wu; Jia-Ni Hu; Bei Yu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present, including appendices and tables.
record.tranche_reason: Tests loss scaling and compute-optimal allocation in native multimodal pre-training using matched image-content and content-free-padding runs, an extension beyond text-only language-model training.
record.gate_note: The study measures smoothed training-loss frontiers as a proxy for test loss and estimates compute-optimal allocations. General-language and spatial benchmark results are not treated as downstream-predictability rows: the paper does not fit or test a prediction law relating those scores to pretraining loss. The reported visual-anchor-gap fits measure relative loss differences, not absolute loss scaling, so they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study fits loss–compute power-law frontiers and compute-optimal allocation exponents for the text and multimodal streams of native multimodal models (71M–3B activated parameters). It reports how the allocation exponent depends on the estimator and how the multimodal-loss exponent depends on visual content. These results bear on V1, V3, V5 and V7 in a new setting.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that visual content lowers multimodal text-prediction loss, with a relative advantage that grows roughly as a power law of compute. Text loss scaling, compute-optimal allocation and aggregate language scores stay largely unchanged. Spatial reasoning improves with scale in both conditions, with selective extra gains from visual content in localization, navigation and symbolic planning.
record.recipe_differences: This is a controlled native-multimodal visual-content ablation using matched IMG and PAD models, multimodal stream loss frontiers, and allocation estimators. It is not a direct reproduction of the original text-only scaling experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The text allocation exponent depends on estimator: IsoFLOP gives 0.649 for IMG and 0.645 for PAD, while the envelope estimator gives 0.578 for both. The paper also reports that fixed-compute visual-anchor gaps depend on model size and that the gap need not be largest at the loss-minimizing allocation.

fits_no_version.finding: The relative multimodal loss gap (PAD vs IMG) grows as a power law of multimodal compute, with γ≈0.254–0.256 (log-space R² 0.955–0.978) across three summaries. A joint fit gives gap ∝ N^0.212 D^0.301.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In matched native-multimodal training, the relative loss benefit of visual content grows approximately as a power law of compute.

record.problems: The loss analysis uses smoothed training loss as a proxy for test loss. Allocation estimators reuse the same runs, so their agreement is not independent validation. The paper notes that gap fits reuse correlated observations and do not establish training-seed reproducibility or behavior beyond the fitted range. No statistical error bars or confidence intervals are reported in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported general-language or spatial benchmark scores are included: the benchmark outcomes do not measure a fitted pretraining-loss or downstream-predictability law. The paper's many benchmark-level scores appear in Tables 5–12 and are outside the versions tested here.

untested.parts: Held-out loss (the study uses smoothed training loss as a proxy). Separate laws in parameters or tokens with the other axes non-bottlenecked. Several orders of magnitude (the fitted compute range is ~1.4 orders). Goodness of fit is not reported.
Entire version: no extrapolation from small runs to larger runs is tested.
Stability of the exponent beyond ~1.5 orders of compute; no fit-quality statistics. The multimodal-stream allocation exponents are shown only in figures, without numbers.
Entire version: no shape variation at fixed parameter count.
Video and other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer. Image-text native pretraining only.
Benchmark scores rise with N and D (Tables 5–12), but no predictive law or loss-to-score relation is fitted.
Parameter-counting conventions, training schedule, and fitting method for the loss frontier. Bending away from a single power law.

missing.what: Multimodal-stream compute-optimal allocation exponents (IsoFLOP and envelope) for IMG and PAD; plotted but not stated numerically in the text.
Paired text anchor gap ranges from −0.095% to +0.128% (mean −0.006%). This confirms that the text frontier does not depend on fitting.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Results come from single training runs, with no error bars. The two allocation estimators reuse the same runs. Removed the reader's V1 limits_scope label (training-loss proxy, per-axis laws): these are untested parts, not qualifying results. Removed the V5 limits_scope label: V5 claims the same form, not the same exponents, and different exponents across conditions are V7 evidence instead.

versions.untested_parts: Uses smoothed training loss as a practical proxy for test loss rather than held-out loss. Does not independently establish power laws in each of parameters, tokens, and compute with the other two non-bottlenecked; the reported loss frontiers are equal-FLOPs envelopes over the tested range.
No explicit prediction of runs orders of magnitude larger from fits to small runs.

Allocation estimates concern the text and multimodal objectives in this fixed native-multimodal setup and mixture; they do not compare arbitrary training setups or validate allocations outside the observed compute range.
No controlled comparison varying depth, width, or other architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
Tests native multimodal image-text pre-training only; does not test video, other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer-training regimes.
Reports downstream benchmark scores across scale, but does not test whether downstream performance is predictably determined by pretraining loss or fit a downstream scaling prediction law.

Shows allocation-exponent sensitivity to the estimator within this study. Does not directly compare parameter-count conventions, schedules, datasets, or fitting choices across the cited language-model studies, and does not test whether curves bend away from a single power law.

rows.subject: A71M–A3B (six-model scaling ladder; aggregate fitted envelope)
rows.operation_detail: Fit power-law loss-compute frontier to the multimodal-objective training-curve envelope for the IMG condition.
rows.measure: Fitted multimodal loss frontier as a function of compute
rows.note: The paper states that the IMG frontier lies below the PAD frontier throughout Cmm ∈ [1.042 × 10^19, 2.504 × 10^20] FLOPs.
rows.check: Also bears on V7: with the same runs and text, removing visual content changes the multimodal loss-decay exponent from 0.129 (IMG) to 0.203 (PAD).

rows.subject: A71M–A3B (six-model scaling ladder; aggregate fitted envelope)
rows.operation_detail: Fit power-law loss-compute frontier to the multimodal-objective training-curve envelope for the PAD condition.
rows.measure: Fitted multimodal loss frontier as a function of compute
rows.note: The paper states that the IMG frontier lies below the PAD frontier throughout the evaluated range.
rows.check: State was wrongly 'partial'. The PAD multimodal frontier is also well summarised by the fitted power-law form; higher loss than IMG is not a weaker power law. PAD has no visual content, so it is a mixed-format training regime rather than another modality. Also bears on V7 through the exponent shift (0.203 vs 0.129).

rows.subject: A71M–A3B (six-model scaling ladder; aggregate paired-gap fit)
rows.operation_detail: Fit compute dependence of the largest paired multimodal visual-anchor gap over supported model sizes.
rows.measure: Relative multimodal loss increase under PAD versus IMG, fitted against compute
rows.value: γmm^max = 0.254; log-space R² = 0.978; fitted gap at 10^20 FLOPs = 0.06231
rows.note: This is a power law for the relative gap, not for absolute loss.
rows.check: Power law in the relative IMG–PAD gap, not in loss; correctly placed under fits_no_version.

rows.subject: A71M–A3B (six-model scaling ladder; aggregate paired-gap fit)
rows.operation_detail: Fit compute dependence of the maximum of a quadratic fit to paired multimodal gaps over model size.
rows.measure: Relative multimodal loss increase under PAD versus IMG, fitted against compute
rows.value: γmm^quad = 0.254; log-space R² = 0.972; fitted gap at 10^20 FLOPs = 0.06212; quadratic maximum rises from 3.63% to 8.09%
rows.note: The endpoint gaps refer to the smallest and largest fitted budgets.

rows.subject: A71M–A3B (six-model scaling ladder; aggregate paired-gap fit)
rows.operation_detail: Fit compute dependence of paired multimodal gaps evaluated along the IMG training-curve envelope.
rows.measure: Relative multimodal loss increase under PAD versus IMG, fitted against compute
rows.value: γmm^loss = 0.256; log-space R² = 0.955; fitted gap at 10^20 FLOPs = 0.06099; gap rises from 3.35% to 8.09%
rows.note: The paired gap uses the model size selected by the IMG envelope, with PAD evaluated at the same allocation.
